result.title: Payoff-Aware Prediction of Population Game Dynamics
result.summary: Population game dynamics describe how aggregate behavior evolves in response to payoff signals. In many applications, the payoff function may change, and the goal is to predict the population trajectory induced by a new payoff design before trajectory data under that design are available. We study this problem as $\textbf{payoff-aware prediction of population game dynamics}$. Standard dynamics learning methods fit the motion observed under training payoffs, but do not separate the payoff-dependent incentive from the payoff-independent response structure needed for prediction under new payoffs. Building on the existing framework of Riemannian game dynamics, we propose PA-RmD, a payoff-aware learning method that keeps payoff information explicit and learns the payoff-independent response structure from data. Theoretically, we show that the learned model preserves fixed-payoff Nash equilibria and derive finite-time one-step prediction bounds under shared-response and payoff-coverage conditions. Empirically, we evaluate PA-RmD on synthetic zero-sum and potential games, as well as a YouTube Trending multi-country dataset, showing that our method performs well under changing payoff designs.

AI.brief_summary: 研究在 payoff 设计改变、新设计下无轨迹数据时预测群体博弈动力学，提出 PA-RmD，显式保留 payoff 信息并仅从数据学习与 payoff 无关的响应结构，并给出不动点保持与有限时间一步预测界。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把「外源 payoff 信号」与「内在响应结构」分离以便在新条件下外推的思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据驱动更新与隐状态自身动力学的解耦，以及对新任务条件推理轨迹的外推预测。
